files.purpose: Defines the whole MCP domain model for Droppy Code: the three transports (stdio/http/oauth), the MCPField input descriptor, the MCPCategory taxonomy, the MCPCatalogEntry shape with its {key} placeholder fill/resolve logic, the resolved-server struct handed to providers and the probe, the persisted MCPConnection record, the probe result and tool summary, the setup-guide and connection-state enums, the MCPPaths file locations for the per-provider config files, and a Color(rgb:) initializer for the 0xRRGGBB brand tints.
key_symbols: enum MCPTransport (Sendable, Hashable): case stdio(command: String, args: [String]), case http(url: String, headers: [String: String]), case oauth(url: String)
struct MCPField (Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable): key, label, placeholder, kind (default .secret), help: String? = nil, defaultValue: String? = nil, isRequired = true; id { key }
enum MCPField.Kind: case secret, text, path

enum MCPCategory: String, CaseIterable, Sendable, Identifiable - developer, browser, search, work, data, cloud, knowledge; id { rawValue }; title switch returning "Developer", "Browser", "Search", "Work", "Data", "Cloud", "Knowledge"

struct MCPCatalogEntry (Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable): id, name, vendor, summary, category, asset, colorValue: UInt32, isMonochrome = false, transport, fields: [MCPField] = [], env: [String: String] = [:], docsURL, sampleTools: [String] = [], keysURL: String? = nil
MCPCatalogEntry.color -> Color { Color(rgb: colorValue) }
MCPCatalogEntry.needsInput -> Bool { fields.contains { $0.isRequired } }
MCPCatalogEntry.isOAuth -> Bool (pattern-matches .oauth on transport)

struct MCPResolvedServer (Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable): id, name, command: String?, args: [String] = [], env: [String: String] = [:], url: String?, headers: [String: String] = [:], oauthUpstream: String?; isRemote { url != nil }
extension MCPCatalogEntry.oauthURL(values: [String: String] = [:]) -> String?
extension MCPCatalogEntry.fill(_ text: String, values: [String: String]) -> String
extension MCPCatalogEntry.resolve(values: [String: String]) -> MCPResolvedServer
struct MCPToolSummary (Codable, Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable): name, summary: String?; id { name }
struct MCPProbeResult (Sendable, Hashable): serverName: String?, serverVersion: String?, tools: [MCPToolSummary]

struct MCPConnection (Codable, Sendable, Hashable, Identifiable): catalogID, isEnabled = true, values: [String: String] = [:], connectedAt: Date?, serverVersion: String?, tools: [MCPToolSummary] = []; id { catalogID }
struct MCPSetupGuide (Sendable, Hashable): title, reason, steps: [String], pageLabel, pageURL, note: String?
enum MCPConnectionState (Sendable, Hashable): notConnected, connecting, connected(toolCount: Int), failed(message: String), needsSetup(MCPSetupGuide); isConnected, isConnecting
enum MCPPaths: static directory, connectionsURL, customsURL, claudeConfigURL, codexConfigURL, copilotConfigURL
extension Color { init(rgb hex: UInt32) }
calls_into: MCPProxy.url(for: id) - used inside resolve() to point an OAuth server's url at the app's local proxy route
Storage.root - base URL for the mcp/ directory, mcp.json and custom-mcp.json
MCPKeychain (named in doc comments as where secret field values live)
MCPKeyPanel (named in the keysURL doc comment as the panel that opens the key page)
MCPOAuth (named in the .oauth transport doc comment as the sign-in implementation)
state_owned: MCPPaths.directory - a lazily-initialized static let URL (Storage.root/mcp, created on first access)
MCPPaths.connectionsURL, customsURL, claudeConfigURL, codexConfigURL, copilotConfigURL - static let URLs
MCPConnection is the persisted per-server user state value type (isEnabled, values, connectedAt, serverVersion, tools)
No ObservableObject or @State here; every type is a value type (struct/enum), all Sendable + Hashable
side_effects: MCPPaths.directory's initializer calls FileManager.default.createDirectory(at:withIntermediateDirectories: true) with try? - it creates Storage.root/mcp on first touch and silently swallows failure
No network, process launch, timers or Keychain access happen in this file itself; it only names the files and the Keychain store that other code uses
platform_assumptions: SwiftUI is imported solely for Color; Color(rgb:) builds a Color from Double components divided by 255 with no explicit color space
Swift concurrency Sendable conformance throughout, plus implicit-return switch bodies (Swift 5.9+) in MCPCategory.title
Storage.root is an app-owned macOS support directory
The generated config files target macOS CLI agents: `claude --mcp-config`, Codex app-server `config` overrides, `copilot --additional-mcp-config`
OAuth servers depend on a local HTTP proxy (MCPProxy) running in-process on the Mac
persisted_fields: Storage.root/mcp.json - JSON for [MCPConnection]; keys: catalogID (String), isEnabled (Bool, default true), values ([String:String], default empty), connectedAt (Date?), serverVersion (String?), tools ([MCPToolSummary], default empty)
Storage.root/custom-mcp.json - JSON for [MCPCustomServer] (secret values never land here)
Storage.root/mcp/codex.json - {"mcp_servers": {...}} for Codex's app-server config overrides
Secret field values are explicitly NOT stored in mcp.json; they live in the Keychain via MCPKeychain
ui_elements: MCPCategory.title strings used as section headings: "Developer", "Browser", "Search", "Work", "Data", "Cloud", "Knowledge"
MCPCatalogEntry.summary is documented as one line shown under the name on its card
MCPCatalogEntry.sampleTools is documented as three or four tools shown as the card's fine print
MCPCatalogEntry.asset names an Assets.xcassets image set of the form `mcp-<id>`, a template SVG tinted with `color`
isMonochrome = true means the brand mark is black or white and wears the text colour instead of colorValue

MCPSetupGuide drives a floating panel offered by the card: title (doc example "Turn on GitLab's MCP server"), reason, ordered steps, pageLabel (doc example "Open my groups"), pageURL, and an optional note shown under the buttons after a check that still fails
MCPConnectionState drives the page and composer display, including connected(toolCount:) and failed(message:)
feature_notes: Tool-call naming: the entry id is the server key in every provider config and therefore the server part of a tool call name, documented with the example `mcp__github__list_issues`; ids must be lowercase with hyphens only
fill() placeholder substitution: every `{key}` in text is replaced by values[key] (an empty string is treated as absent) else field.defaultValue else the empty string

Host-coercion rule in fill(): when a placeholder sits immediately after "://" (the test is `out.contains("://" + token)`), the value is trimmed of whitespace and newlines, a leading "https://" or "http://" is dropped (case-insensitive prefix test on the lowercased value), and all trailing "/" are removed - so pasting `https://gitlab.example.com/` yields `gitlab.example.com`

resolve() for .stdio: sets command, maps args through fill, and sets env = env.mapValues(fill).filter { !$0.value.isEmpty } so an optional field left empty drops its variable rather than passing an empty string
resolve() for .http: url = fill(url) and headers = headers.mapValues(fill) with empty values dropped the same way

resolve() for .oauth: server.url = MCPProxy.url(for: id) and server.oauthUpstream = fill(url) - the provider config never sees the real remote address, and no token ever sits in a config file because the proxy adds a fresh token per request
needsInput is true only when at least one field has isRequired == true, so an optional key (one that merely raises a rate limit) does not make a server need input
MCPConnectionState.isConnecting is implemented as `self == .connecting`, relying on the enum's synthesized Equatable
Color(rgb:) decodes 0xRRGGBB as red = (hex >> 16) & 0xFF / 255, green = (hex >> 8) & 0xFF / 255, blue = hex & 0xFF / 255
unresolved_questions: The `extension MCPCatalogEntry` block opens with a doc comment ("The launchable form, with `{key}` placeholders replaced by the user's values (or the field's default). OAuth servers resolve to their route on the app's proxy.") separated by a blank line from oauthURL's own doc comment, so it documents nothing; it reads like resolve()'s documentation stranded by a reordering, but intent cannot be confirmed from this file.
MCPProxy.url(for:) route shape, MCPOAuth's token flow, MCPKeychain's key naming and Storage.root's concrete path are all defined outside this bundle.
Whether Color(rgb:) yields sRGB or SwiftUI's default color space is not stated; Color(red:green:blue:) is called without a color space argument.

files.purpose: The hard-coded catalog of the 33 MCP servers Droppy Code ships with: each entry's id, display name, vendor, one-line summary, category, asset name, brand colour, transport (exact command and args, or exact remote URL and headers), credential fields with placeholder and help text, environment variables, docs URL, sample tool names and key-creation page. It also provides lookup by id, tolerant lookup by server name, a grouped-by-category view and the flat id list.

byCategory walks MCPCategory.allCases in declaration order (developer, browser, search, work, data, cloud, knowledge), compactMaps away empty groups, and preserves each entry's catalog order inside its group

files.purpose: Models user-defined MCP servers from Settings > MCP > Custom: the lean Codable MCPCustomServer record (stdio or http, with named env or header variables flagged secret or not), its tolerant decoder, its slugged `custom-` id generator, its one-line card summary, the bridge that turns it into a synthetic MCPCatalogEntry so the rest of the MCP machinery treats it as built-in, and the MCPCustomError validation enum with its exact user-facing messages, variable-key rule and remote-URL rule.

platform_assumptions: URL.host() is the modern parenthesized Foundation API (macOS 13+), not the deprecated `host` property

The variable-key rule (a letter or underscore first) follows Unix environment-variable naming conventions
Implicit-return switch expressions in the Kind-switching computed properties require Swift 5.9+
persisted_fields: custom-mcp.json entries use exactly the CodingKeys: id (String, required), name (String, required), kind (String enum "stdio" | "http", required), command (String, missing -> ""), args ([String], missing -> []), env ([Variable], missing -> []), url (String, missing -> ""), headers ([Variable], missing -> [])
Variable is persisted as {"key": String, "isSecret": Bool}; isSecret defaults to false in memory but Variable uses the synthesized decoder, so the JSON key is expected to be present
id format: "custom-" + slug, e.g. "custom-my-server"; a name with no letters or digits yields exactly "custom-server"
Variable values are deliberately not persisted in this record: non-secret values go to mcp.json (MCPConnection.values) and secret ones to the Keychain
ui_elements: Card line for a stdio server: "Runs on this Mac: <command> <args joined with single spaces>." with a trailing period
Card line for an http server: "Remote server at <host>." with a trailing period, falling back to the raw url string when URL parsing yields no host

Error messages verbatim: "The server needs a name."; "A server named \u201C<name>\u201D already exists."; "A stdio server needs a command."; "The URL must start with https:// (or http:// for a local server)."; "\u201C<key>\u201D is not a valid variable name: letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, starting with a letter or `_`."; "\u201C<key>\u201D is listed twice." - the quotes are curly typographic quotes and the message body contains literal backticks
Custom entries render with vendor "Custom", asset "" (no image), colorValue 0 and isMonochrome true, so they wear the text colour rather than a brand tint
Each variable becomes an MCPField whose label is the key itself and whose placeholder is the empty string; kind is .secret when isSecret is true, otherwise .text
catalogEntry() sets docsURL to the empty string, so a custom server has no documentation link
feature_notes: makeID slugging: lowercases the name, keeps letters and digits, collapses every run of other characters into a single "-", never emits a leading dash (lastWasDash starts as true), strips a trailing dash, then prefixes "custom-"; an unsluggable name such as "!!!" falls back to "custom-server"

catalogEntry() builds placeholders as a dictionary mapping each variable key to "{key}", deduplicated with uniquingKeysWith { first, _ in first } because drafts reach the editor's header before duplicate keys are validated

For stdio the placeholders dictionary is assigned to entry.env after construction; for http it is passed as the transport's headers - either way MCPCatalogEntry.fill/resolve substitutes the user's typed values exactly as for a built-in server

validate() order: trim the name and reject empty (.emptyName); compute makeID(name) and reject when existingIDs contains it (.takenName with the trimmed name); then the kind-specific check (stdio: trimmed command must be non-empty else .emptyCommand; http: validRemoteURL else .badURL); then walk variables checking validVariableKey and uniqueness; returns nil when the server is savable

Duplicate detection is case-insensitive for http headers (the key is lowercased before insertion into the seen set) and case-sensitive for stdio env vars, matching HTTP header semantics versus Unix env var semantics
validVariableKey: the first character must be a letter or "_", and every character must be a letter, a number, "_", "-" or "."; an empty key fails because key.first is nil

validRemoteURL: trims whitespace and newlines, requires URLComponents to parse with a scheme and a non-empty host; the lowercased scheme must be "https" or "http"; "http" is accepted only when the lowercased host is one of "localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1" or "[::1]"; "https" is accepted for any host

The tolerant decoder requires only id, name and kind and defaults every other field, so a definition saved before a field existed (or hand-edited) loads with the missing pieces empty rather than dropping the whole list
variables returns the kind-appropriate list, so switching a draft between stdio and http swaps which variable list the editor and catalogEntry() read without discarding the other one
unresolved_questions: takenName is checked only against the caller-supplied existingIDs set; whether that set includes MCPCatalog.ids (so a custom cannot shadow a built-in id) is decided by the caller, outside this bundle.

Variable has no custom decoder, so a stored variable object missing "isSecret" would throw during decoding rather than default to false, and because the throw happens inside decodeIfPresent([Variable]...) it would fail the whole server record; whether the app ever writes such JSON cannot be determined from this file.
Where custom servers are loaded and saved (MCPPaths.customsURL) and how the editor surfaces MCPCustomError.message are in files outside this bundle.
